issues.description: The template's Farm.java file contains an incorrect class declaration and invalid syntax that conflict with the problem specification and will prevent students from compiling or implementing the intended design. The file declares 'public class AnimalFarm' instead of 'public class Farm', includes a duplicated 'package' declaration inside a method, and has malformed/duplicated class braces and methods. This deviates from the UML and the solution (which expects a class named Farm with a List<Animal> attribute and specific methods) and will confuse or block students attempting to follow the exercise.
issues.suggestedFix: Replace the broken Farm.java with a proper Farm class skeleton matching the problem UML: declare 'public class Farm' in package de.tum.cit.ase, remove any nested/duplicate package declarations, and provide the expected fields and method stubs (private List<Animal> animals; public Farm() { this.animals = new ArrayList<>(); } getters/setters, addAnimal(Animal), feedAllAnimals(), singFarmSong() and a private singFarmSongVerse(Animal) helper). Ensure the file compiles so students can implement the bodies according to the specification.

issues.description: The problem statement and solution refer to a class named 'Farm', but the template file at src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java declares a class named 'AnimalFarm'. This mismatch between the expected class name (Farm) and the template's class name (AnimalFarm) creates a mapping barrier: students are instructed to implement/extend/instantiate 'Farm' while the starter file contains 'AnimalFarm', which may prevent compilation and confuse which class to implement.
issues.suggestedFix: Rename the class in the template file src/de/tum/cit/ase/Farm.java from 'AnimalFarm' to 'Farm' (i.e., change the class declaration to 'public class Farm') so the template matches the problem statement and the solution. Ensure the file name and public class name are consistent to avoid compilation and conceptual mapping issues.
